note: Dynamic keyword knowledge base. Add entries here (or to the kb_entries MongoDB collection) — the engine reloads on file change without a deploy. Answers are plain-language, 2-4 sentences, with a concrete next step.

entries.answer: An eviction or 'quit' notice starts a clock — read it for the exact deadline and amount claimed. Do not ignore it. Call 211 today for free legal aid, and contact your landlord in writing to request a payment plan or proof of any balance. Keep every notice and receipt.

Landlords are generally required to keep a home safe and habitable — heat, water, and working locks are basic rights. Put your repair request in writing and keep a copy. If the landlord ignores you, call 211 for local tenant rights help or your city's housing department. Do not withhold rent without legal advice first.

Most states require landlords to return a security deposit within a set time and give an itemized list for any deductions. Ask in writing for your deposit and itemized deductions, and take photos of the unit when you leave. If they refuse, call 211 or your state's tenant rights office — small claims court is an option.

Rent increases are regulated in many places — the landlord must usually give written notice and can't raise rent mid-lease. Check your lease and your local rent rules. Call 211 to find rental assistance programs, and if the increase is illegal, contact your city's tenant protection office.

For rental assistance or shelter, call 211 — they keep a live list of shelters, housing vouchers, and rental help in your area. Section 8 (housing choice vouchers) applications open periodically through your local housing authority. If you are at risk of homelessness tonight, call 211 now for a shelter bed and support.

Tenants have basic rights everywhere: a habitable home, privacy with proper notice, and protection against illegal eviction. The exact rules vary by state and city. Call 211 to reach a tenant-rights organization or legal aid, and keep written records of everything with your landlord.

Free and low-cost legal help exists. Call 211 to find legal aid organizations in your area, or visit LawHelp.org and enter your state. Many courthouses have self-help centers that explain forms and procedures for free. Never sign anything you do not understand without asking questions first.

Small claims court handles many disputes without lawyers — usually under a few thousand dollars. File at the courthouse in the county where the other party lives or where the issue happened. The clerk's office and the court's self-help center can walk you through the forms. Ask 211 for free legal aid to prepare.

If you are charged with a crime, you have the right to a lawyer — ask the court for a public defender if you cannot afford one, at your first court date. Do not speak to police or prosecutors without your lawyer present. Write down everything and keep your court dates; missing one can make things worse.

For legal documents like a power of attorney or will, free or low-cost help is available: call 211 for legal aid, or check your local library and senior center for free notary and legal clinics. Banks and credit unions often notarize for free for members. Never sign a legal document you do not fully understand.

Immigration matters are high-stakes — only an accredited immigration lawyer or DOJ-accredited representative should advise you. Call 211 for free immigration legal services, or find accredited help at immigrationlawhelp.org. If you have a hearing or deadline, never miss it, and never sign anything without legal help.

The IRS will work with you — you can set up a payment plan or apply for hardship status. Respond to any IRS letter by its deadline; ignoring it adds penalties. Never pay anyone who calls claiming to be the IRS demanding payment — the IRS sends letters, not calls. Visit IRS.gov or call 1-800-829-1040 directly.

Debt collectors must follow the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act: they can't harass you, call at odd hours, or lie about what you owe. You have the right to request written verification of the debt in writing. Do not give bank or card numbers to a caller — verify the debt first. Call 211 for free credit and debt counseling.

You can check your credit for free every week at AnnualCreditReport.com. If something is wrong, dispute it in writing with the credit bureaus — they must investigate. Building credit takes time: pay on time, keep balances low, and avoid payday loans. Call 211 for free financial counseling.

You can open a bank account even with a low balance or past bank issues — look for second-chance checking accounts or credit unions. If your account is frozen, contact the bank in writing to find out why. Never pay overdraft fees you can't verify — banks must honor errors you report in writing.

Payday and title loans carry extremely high interest and can trap you in debt. Before taking one, call 211 for free financial counseling and local emergency assistance — grants and interest-free help often exist. If you already owe, contact the lender about a payment plan and get free credit counseling.

A wage garnishment means a court ordered part of your paycheck withheld for a debt. You can often challenge it or reduce it — respond to court paperwork immediately and file a claim of exemption. Call 211 for free legal aid; legal aid lawyers stop garnishments every day.

Bankruptcy is a legal process that can discharge or reorganize debt — but it is serious and affects your credit for years. Consult a bankruptcy attorney or free legal aid first; many consultations are free. Do not pay a company to file for you when legal aid or a licensed attorney can do it for less.

You can file your taxes for free through IRS Free File if your income qualifies, and VITA (Volunteer Income Tax Assistance) provides free in-person tax help — find a site near you at IRS.gov/vita. Do not pay a refund-advance company for money you can get free. Keep all tax documents for at least 3 years.

SNAP (food stamps) helps with groceries — apply online at your state's benefits portal or benefits.gov. You will need ID, income info, and bills. Approval is often quick, and benefits load onto an EBT card. Call 211 if you need help applying or your application was denied.

WIC provides food, formula, and nutrition support for pregnant women, new mothers, and young children. Apply through your local WIC office or call 211 for the nearest location. WIC covers formula, milk, eggs, and more, and it is free for qualifying families.

Medicaid provides free or low-cost health coverage for qualifying low-income adults, children, pregnant women, and people with disabilities. Apply online at healthcare.gov or your state's Medicaid website. Coverage can be retroactive, so apply as soon as you need care. Call 211 for application help.

Medicare covers people 65 and older and some younger people with disabilities. Sign up during your Initial Enrollment Period — the 7 months around your 65th birthday — to avoid late penalties. Visit Medicare.gov or call 1-800-MEDICARE (1-800-633-4227) for free help choosing plans.

SSI and SSDI are Social Security programs for people with disabilities. Apply at ssa.gov or call 1-800-772-1213 — you can apply online and by phone. Gather medical records before applying; denials are common, so appeal within 60 days. Free legal help with appeals: call 211.

You can manage Social Security retirement benefits at ssa.gov — check your statement, estimate benefits, and apply online. Never give your Social Security number to anyone who calls you. For help, call 1-800-772-1213 or your local Social Security office (appointments recommended).

File for unemployment the week you lose work — most states have a one-week waiting period and strict deadlines. Apply on your state's Department of Labor website, and keep filing weekly claims even while you look for work. If your claim is denied, appeal — many denials are overturned.

TANF provides temporary cash assistance for families with children, and many states also offer emergency assistance programs. Apply through your state's benefits office or call 211 to be screened for cash, rent, and utility help. Keep copies of everything you submit.

LIHEAP helps low-income households pay heating and cooling bills and can prevent shutoffs. Apply through your state's LIHEAP office (find it at acf.hhs.gov/liheap). If you have a shut-off notice, call 211 immediately — emergency programs can stop disconnections.

Being fired is stressful, but you have options. File for unemployment right away — do not wait, there are deadlines. If you believe the firing was illegal (discrimination, retaliation, or unpaid wages), contact your state labor board or call 211 for free legal help. Keep any emails, pay stubs, and written communications.

If you were laid off, file for unemployment immediately and ask about severance in writing. Review any separation agreement carefully before signing — you may be giving up rights. Call 211 for free legal aid to review severance, and update your resume and job search profiles right away.

You have a right to every dollar you earned — including overtime and tips. Contact your state labor department or the U.S. Department of Labor (dol.gov, 1-866-487-9243) and file a wage claim; it is free. Do not wait — wage claims have deadlines. Call 211 for free employment legal help.

It is illegal to fire or refuse to hire someone because of race, sex, religion, disability, age, or other protected status. File a charge with the EEOC (eeoc.gov, 1-800-669-4000) or your state civil rights agency — there are strict deadlines. Call 211 for free legal help.

Apply for unemployment on your state's labor department website. If denied, appeal within the deadline shown on the denial letter — most appeals are decided by phone or mail. Bring pay stubs and your termination notice. Call 211 for help with the application and appeal.

Free and low-cost job training exists through your state's workforce board, community colleges, and programs like Goodwill and Urban League. Call 211 for local training programs, or ask your local library about free certification courses. Many programs pay you while you train.

Gig workers are often independent contractors — meaning no employer withholding, and you owe estimated taxes yourself. Set aside money for taxes, track mileage and expenses, and check if your state offers contractor protections. If a gig platform owes you pay, file a claim with your state labor board.

Never ignore a medical bill — hospitals and clinics often have charity care and payment plans that can reduce or erase what you owe. Ask the billing office for financial assistance in writing, and request an itemized bill. Call 211 for help finding charity care programs and free financial counseling.

If your health insurance denies a claim, you have the right to appeal — usually several times. Start the appeal in writing by the deadline in the denial letter, and ask your doctor to support it. Your state's insurance department can also help with denials. Call 211 for a free patient advocate.

Ask your pharmacist about generics, patient assistance programs, and discount cards like GoodRx — prices vary by pharmacy, so compare. Many drug makers have free-medication programs for people who qualify. Never skip doses because of cost without asking your doctor for alternatives.

People with both Medicare and Medicaid (dual-eligible) can get extra help with premiums, copays, and drugs. Apply for Medicare Savings Programs through your state Medicaid office — they can save you thousands a year. Call 211 for application help.

Free and sliding-scale mental health help exists: call 988 for crisis support, and call 211 for low-cost counseling in your area. Federally funded health centers charge based on income, and many therapists offer sliding scales. If you are in crisis, call or text 988 now — it is free and confidential.

Recovery support is available at every stage. Call 1-800-662-HELP (SAMHSA's free, confidential helpline) 24/7 for treatment and support options, or call 211 for local programs. You do not need insurance to start — many programs are free or sliding-scale. Asking for help is strength.

Federally qualified health centers and dental schools offer low-cost dental care, and many communities hold free dental clinics. Call 211 for local options. For severe pain or swelling, do not wait — emergency rooms and urgent care treat dental emergencies, and hospitals cannot turn you away in an emergency.

Childcare assistance programs subsidize daycare for working families — apply through your state's childcare subsidy office. Head Start and Early Head Start offer free preschool for income-eligible families. Call 211 to find local providers and application help.

Child support and custody are handled through family court — you do not need a lawyer to start, but free legal aid helps. Apply for child support enforcement through your state's child support agency, which can garnish wages. Call 211 for free family law help in your area.

Help for seniors and caregivers exists: call your local Area Agency on Aging (find it at eldercare.acl.gov or call 1-800-677-1116) for meals, home care, and benefits help. Medicaid covers some long-term care. Call 211 for local caregiver support groups and respite services.

Services for people with disabilities — including home care and respite — are available through your state's disability agency. Call 211 to find local resources, or contact your state's Department of Developmental Services. Free legal help with rights and benefits: call 211 for a disability rights organization.

You do not have to face this alone. Call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233 (text START to 88788) — free, confidential, 24/7. They can connect you to shelter, safety planning, and legal help. If you are in immediate danger, call 911. You deserve safety.

Call Poison Control immediately at 1-800-222-1222 — it is free, confidential, and available 24/7. If someone stops breathing or collapses, call 911 first. Do not induce vomiting unless Poison Control tells you to. Save the product bottle to read ingredients.

In an immediate emergency, call 911. For disaster help, register with FEMA at DisasterAssistance.gov or call 1-800-621-3362 — they can help with temporary housing and repairs. Call 211 for shelter, food, and recovery resources in your area.

GED prep and testing is free or low-cost in most states — contact your local adult education center, community college, or library. Many programs include free practice tests and paid testing vouchers. Call 211 for the nearest free GED program.

Free English classes (ESL/ESOL) are offered by libraries, community colleges, and community centers across the country. Ask your local library for their schedule, or call 211 for programs near you. Many also offer citizenship classes and conversation groups.

Start with the FAFSA at studentaid.gov — it unlocks Pell Grants (money you do not repay), work-study, and loans. Fill it out even if you think you make too much; community colleges and trade schools accept it too. Get free FAFSA help from your school's financial aid office — never pay someone to file it for you.

On this platform, the Learn section offers free courses, labs, and credentials — check /courses and /labs. Beyond here, many libraries give free access to online learning platforms. You do not need to pay to start learning.

If you cannot afford your federal student loan payments, apply for an Income-Driven Repayment plan or deferment at studentaid.gov — do not ignore the bills. Public service and teacher loan forgiveness exist for qualifying work. Free help: your loan servicer and studentaid.gov, never a paid 'loan forgiveness' company.

Act fast: freeze your credit at AnnualCreditReport.com (all three bureaus), place a fraud alert, and report to IdentityTheft.gov. Contact your bank about the fraudulent charges immediately. The FTC's IdentityTheft.gov walks you through a step-by-step recovery plan for free.

Real agencies never call demanding payment — hang up. Add your number to the Do Not Call registry (donotcall.gov) and block the number. Report scam calls to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. Never give personal or banking info to an unexpected caller.

You never pay to collect a prize — anyone asking you to wire money, send gift cards, or pay 'fees' to claim a win is a scam. Legitimate lotteries deduct from winnings. Hang up, do not send money, and report it at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

The 'grandparent scam' is common: a caller pretends to be a relative in jail or trouble and demands bail money, often gift cards. Verify independently — call your relative directly on a number you know. Never send gift cards or wire money to an unknown caller. Report it to the FTC.

Be very cautious if someone you met online asks for money, gifts, or crypto — especially before meeting in person. Romance scammers build trust over weeks then invent emergencies. Never send money to someone you have not met in person. Report it at ReportFraud.ftc.gov and stop contact.

No one can legally remove accurate negative items from your credit — anyone promising that is a scam. You can dispute errors yourself for free at the credit bureaus. Beware companies charging upfront fees. Free help: AnnualCreditReport.com and 211 for nonprofit credit counseling.

If your utility is at risk of shutoff, call the company TODAY — many states require them to offer payment plans and protect customers in extreme weather. Apply for LIHEAP through your state. Call 211 immediately for emergency utility assistance funds.

The federal Lifeline program discounts phone service, and the Affordable Connectivity Program helps with internet for qualifying households. Apply at lifelinesupport.org and check with your internet provider for low-income plans. Call 211 for help applying.

Food banks and pantries serve anyone who needs them — no questions asked at most. Find the nearest one by calling 211 or visiting FeedingAmerica.org. Many also offer hot meals, senior boxes, and school-weekend programs for kids.

Many communities offer discounted bus passes, medical transport, and ride programs for seniors, disabled people, and low-income workers. Call 211 for transportation help in your area, and ask your caseworker or clinic about ride programs.

Free clothing closets, school-uniform programs, and coat drives exist in most communities. Call 211 for locations near you, and check churches, community centers, and local schools — many run free clothing closets year-round.

Federal programs must provide free interpreters — hospitals, courts, and government offices are required to help you in your language. Ask for an interpreter; it is your right and it is free. Call 211, which offers help in many languages.

If this is an emergency, call 911. For crisis support, call or text 988 (Suicide and Crisis Lifeline) — free and confidential, 24/7. For non-emergency help finding local resources, call 211. You are not alone.

Calling 211 connects you to free local help — housing, food, legal, health, benefits, and more. It is free, confidential, and available 24/7 in most areas, with interpreters for many languages. You can also visit 211.org to search by ZIP code.

This platform combines learning, community, music, games, and AI-assisted creation with the M.O.R.E. Help Center's mission of practical help for everyday life. The Learn section has free courses, labs, and credentials. Create a free account to get started.

Creating an account is free, and the free tier includes courses, community, music, games, and the knowledge base. Paid membership tiers (Member, Plus, Pro, Patron) add more capabilities. AI features run on your own key via the $3 BYOK unlock — the platform does not fund AI for customers.

Click 'Register' in the top menu, enter your name and email, and choose a password. You must be at least 13 years old. After registering you will land on your dashboard where Learn, Community, Music, Games, and your profile are ready to use.

Use the 'Sign In' button with the email and password you registered with. If you are logged out or stuck, use 'Forgot Password' to reset by email. If you still cannot log in, clear your browser cache or use the Help Center.

intents: how do i reset my password
entries.answer: Click 'Forgot Password' on the login page, enter your email, and follow the reset link we send. Choose a strong password you do not reuse elsewhere. If the email does not arrive, check spam and allow a few minutes.

Check the inbox of the email you registered with for a verification link, and check spam/junk if it is not there. Clicking the link confirms your address. If the link expired, request a new one from your profile settings.

You can delete your account from Account Settings → Delete Account. This removes your personal data per our Privacy Policy (see /privacy). Export your data first if you want a copy. Paid subscriptions should be cancelled separately from the payment provider.

Your Account Settings has an 'Export Data' option that produces a JSON copy of your profile and account data. Use it before deleting your account if you want a personal archive. See our Privacy Policy at /privacy for details.

Open your Profile or Settings page and edit your name, email, and avatar there. Email changes may require verification. If you need to update the email on a paid subscription, contact the payment provider or support.

You can review and accept the Terms of Service at /terms and our Privacy Policy at /privacy. Acceptance is recorded on your account. We will notify you of material changes and ask you to accept updated terms.

intents: what does the plus tier include
what does the member tier include
what does the pro tier include
entries.answer: The tiers are Free, Member, Plus, Pro, Patron, and Executive (customer). Each paid tier includes everything below it plus its own features. See the Plans page (/plans) for the current feature list and prices. AI features are not included in any customer tier — AI runs on your own key through the $3 BYOK unlock.

Visit the Plans page (/plans), choose the tier you want, and complete checkout with our payment provider. Your features unlock automatically once the payment is confirmed. You can upgrade or change plans at any time.

You can cancel your subscription at any time from your account or the payment provider's customer portal. Cancellation stops future renewals; features unlocked by the subscription remain until the end of the billing period, then revert. See /refund-policy for refund rules.

You can downgrade or switch plans from the Plans page or the payment provider's portal. When you move to a lower tier, features above your tier become unavailable. Paid-to-free downgrades revert to the free tier at the end of your current period.

The Executive tier is the highest customer membership and includes the features configured for it. Note: being an Executive-tier customer does NOT grant staff or internal systems — internal tools like Arena are restricted to authorized admin/executive staff roles only.

BYOK means 'Bring Your Own Key': for a one-time $3 unlock, you attach your own free API key (Groq, Cerebras, or Gemini) and your AI requests run on YOUR key — not on platform-funded AI. The platform does not fund AI for customers at any tier; BYOK is how customers use AI here.

On the BYOK page (/byok), complete the $3 unlock, then paste a free API key from one of the supported providers (Groq, Cerebras, or Gemini). Your AI conversations then route through your key. You can swap or remove your key anytime from the same page.

intents: where do i get a key
entries.answer: Each provider issues keys free from their console: Groq at console.groq.com, Cerebras at cloud.cerebras.ai, and Gemini at aistudio.google.com. Create a free account, generate an API key, and paste it into the BYOK page. Keys are encrypted at rest and never shown back to you.

BYOK is a one-time $3 unlock for customers. It is not a subscription and not a tier — it is an entitlement that lets you use AI with your own key. Staff roles receive BYOK free as part of their role. See /byok for current details.

Refunds are issued as site credit unless the failure was the platform's fault (see /refund-policy). If your $3 BYOK unlock is refunded, the entitlement is reverted and your AI returns to the knowledge-base fallback until you reactivate.

AI runs on real computing resources that cost money. To keep the platform free and sustainable, the platform does not fund AI for customers — customers who want AI use their own key through the $3 BYOK unlock, and everyone else gets the free knowledge base. Paid tiers fund features, not AI tokens.

AI features on this platform run on YOUR key once you activate the $3 BYOK unlock (/byok). Without BYOK, AI surfaces answer from the knowledge base. This keeps AI honest and free to use for everyone — your key, your usage.

Anonymous visitors do not get AI — AI requires a registered account with the BYOK unlock. Public visitors can use the knowledge base and the site's free content. Create a free account and add your own key at /byok to use AI.

intents: which ai can i talk to
entries.answer: After unlocking BYOK, eligible AI features are available in the AI Console. Each feature is governed by the platform's feature configuration — your tier and role determine what you can use. Internal personas are not available to customers.

AI costs are covered by your own BYOK key, never by the platform for customers. The platform only funds AI for authorized admin/executive staff. If you want more AI capacity, upgrade your own provider key or provider plan — the platform does not pay for customer AI usage.

The Learn section (/courses) lists free courses, modules, and labs with certificates and credentials. Browse, open a course, and work through the modules at your own pace. Progress is saved to your account automatically.
Courses are organized into modules — short units with content and exercises. Open a course in Learn, then click a module to start. Your progress and completions appear in your dashboard.

Labs are hands-on practice exercises tied to courses — try them from the Learn section (/labs). Simulations offer real-world scenarios to practice safely. Lab completions count toward your certificates.

Completing required courses and labs unlocks certificates and credentials in the Learn section. View and download them from your credentials page. Certificates are issued based on verified completion, not automatically.
Tracks are guided learning paths that group courses toward a goal, and the adaptive path adjusts to your progress. Find them in the Learn section. Track completion applies toward related credentials.

The Community section is where members post, discuss, and share. Create a post, comment, and engage — every community has a code of conduct, and reported content is reviewed. Be respectful; harassment gets accounts suspended.

The leaderboard shows top community and game scores for everyone to see. Play games and participate in community activities to climb it. Scores are earned through real activity — there are no paid shortcuts.

Use the report button on any post to flag content for review, and use profile settings to block users who bother you. Reports are reviewed by the moderation team. For urgent safety concerns, contact support directly and call 911 if you are in danger.

Band on a Page lets you create a music page for your band with your tracks and info. It is available at the appropriate membership tier in the Music section. Uploads are governed by the platform's media rules.
Playlist Manager in the Music section lets you curate and organize tracks into playlists. It is available at the appropriate membership tier. Your playlists save to your account.

Music uploads are handled through the Music section at the appropriate tier. Uploaded audio is stored securely and served with preview limits for non-owners. Make sure you have the rights to every track you upload.
The Games section has interactive games tied to learning and community. Scores feed the leaderboard. Open Games from your sidebar and pick a game to play.
Your game scores appear on your dashboard and the community leaderboard. Scores update after each game. Only verified play counts — no automated or scripted scores.
The Sanctuary is a focused space for deeper work and reflection, available at the appropriate tier. See the Sanctuary section in your sidebar for what is included at your tier.

The Store carries digital products — workbooks, courses, and more. Physical merchandise like t-shirts is listed but not sold online yet. Purchases are processed through our payment provider and delivered to your account automatically.

Physical merchandise (t-shirts, printed workbooks, kits) is shown in the store but is not available for online purchase yet — we have not wired up fulfillment. Digital versions of the workbooks are available. Check the product page for the current status.

Checkout runs through our payment provider (Lemon Squeezy or Gumroad). Choose the product, complete the secure checkout, and your entitlement activates automatically once payment is confirmed. If checkout fails, try again or contact support — you are never charged twice.

Subscriptions renew automatically until cancelled. You can cancel anytime from your account or the payment provider's customer portal; cancellation stops future renewals. Features stay active through the paid period, then revert. See /refund-policy.

intents: how do i get a refund
entries.answer: Refunds are issued as site credit unless the failure was the platform's fault — platform-caused failures are refunded to the original payment method. See /refund-policy for the full policy and how to request a refund. Refunded purchases have their entitlements reverted.

Site credit is issued for approved refunds and is applied automatically to your next eligible purchase. It is not cash and cannot be withdrawn; it can only be used on the platform. See /refund-policy for details.
Your payment history and receipts are available in your account's payment history page. For tax documents or detailed invoices, use the payment provider's customer portal, which has the full record.

Payments are processed by Lemon Squeezy (primary) or Gumroad (fallback) — we do not handle card numbers directly. You will see their branded checkout and receipts. Contact them through their portal for payment-method changes.

Scholarship applications are submitted through the Scholarships section. Applications are reviewed by the scholarship committee. Sponsors fund milestone-based releases so funds follow real progress. See /scholarships/apply to start.

Sponsors can fund a scholar through the sponsor page — full, partial, or collective. Sponsorship is milestone-based: funds release as the scholar makes real progress, and you can track milestones in your sponsor view.

Our Privacy Policy at /privacy explains what we collect (name, email, progress), how it is used, and your rights including access, deletion, and export. We do not sell personal data. AI conversation content goes to the AI providers when you use BYOK — see the policy.

The Terms of Service at /terms cover account rules, acceptable use, AI-generated content, payments, and user content. You must be at least 13. Breaking the rules can lead to suspension. We may update terms with notice.

The full Refund Policy is at /refund-policy: refunds are issued as site credit unless the failure was the platform's fault, in which case we refund the original payment method. Subscriptions cancel at any time and stop future renewals.

We use only essential cookies for authentication and security — no tracking or advertising cookies. You can decline cookies and still use the site; you will just need to log in each session. See /privacy for details.
You must be at least 13 years old to create an account, per our Terms and COPPA. If we learn a user is under 13, we delete the account promptly. Parents with questions can contact the Help Center.

The Help Center (/help-center) has answers and contact options. For account, payment, or technical issues, open a support request there — include your account email and a description. For life emergencies, call 911 or 988; for local resources, call 211.

211 is a free, confidential, 24/7 phone line that connects you to local services — housing, food, legal aid, health, benefits, utilities, and more. Dial 2-1-1 from any phone or visit 211.org to search by ZIP code. Interpreters are available in many languages.
988 is the Suicide and Crisis Lifeline — call or text 988 for free, confidential support 24/7. It is for anyone in emotional distress or crisis. If you are in immediate danger, call 911.

Arena is an internal executive system used by authorized staff to refine the platform's capabilities. It is not a customer feature, not a paid tier feature, and not available to members at any tier. If you believe you should have access, contact your administrator.
Jamil is an internal platform persona used by authorized staff. Customer AI features run through your own BYOK key in the AI Console. Jamil is not available to customers.

Command Center, Orchestrator, and other internal systems are restricted to authorized staff roles. Customer accounts cannot access them regardless of tier. Contact your administrator if you believe you should have staff access.
Your dashboard is your home after signing in — it shows your progress, quick links, and account summary. Public visitors see the landing page instead; the dashboard requires an account.

The sidebar shows what you have access to: Learn, Community, Music, Games, and more appear based on your tier and role. If a feature is not in your sidebar, it is likely above your current tier — see /plans to compare. Staff and admin sections appear only for those roles.

The sidebar shows only what your current tier and role unlock. Higher-tier features are intentionally not shown until you upgrade — see /plans for what each tier adds. If you believe something is wrong, check your profile tier and contact support.

The knowledge base answers common questions instantly and free — housing, legal, benefits, payments, and platform how-tos — without any AI cost. AI surfaces use it whenever live AI is not available (no BYOK, no staff access, provider outage, or budget exhausted).

If live AI is unavailable — provider outage, budget, or no BYOK key — you still get a helpful knowledge-base answer instead of nothing. Check your BYOK key status on the /byok page, and try again shortly. Platform features like courses and community are unaffected.
